topStories.headline: Ellis County Incumbents Hold Off Challengers in Tuesday's General Election
topStories.dek: Unofficial results show every Ellis County incumbent survived November 3, though the Precinct 4 commissioner race was decided by fewer than 500 votes.
topStories.body:
Unofficial results posted by the Ellis County Elections Administrator show that all four contested local races on the November 3 ballot were won by sitting officeholders, though one came down to the wire. In the race for County Commissioner, Precinct 4, incumbent Republican Kyle Butler led Democrat Oyinkansola Jinadu by 50.43 percent to 49.57 percent — a margin of roughly 235 votes — in what the Waxahachie Sun reported was among the closest countywide results in recent memory. Jinadu, who ran an active door-to-door campaign, acknowledged the unofficial tally in a public statement but noted that nearly 13,700 voters supported her bid.

In the County Commissioner, Precinct 2 race, incumbent Republican Matt Zajic won with 64.69 percent against write-in candidate Hannah Shelby, who captured 33.78 percent. Republican State Representative Brian Harrison held District 10 with 54.34 percent over Democratic challenger Michael Myers. Republican Justice of the Peace James "Butch" Bryant retained his Precinct 4 seat with 54.29 percent over Democrat Pam Hampton.

In the federal race touching Ellis County, Republican Congressman Jake Ellzey defeated Democratic challenger Danny Minton in Texas' 6th Congressional District. Ellis County voters favored Ellzey by roughly 68.6 percent to 31.4 percent, though Ellzey's district-wide margin was far narrower. The Ellis County Elections Office noted that official results will not be final until all ballot deadlines have passed — six days after Election Day — and all provisional and cured ballots are counted. Official canvassing is expected after November 9.

topStories.headline: Ground Broken on New $10.8 Million Fire Station #1 as Old Downtown Building Shows Its Age
topStories.dek: Construction is under way on a modern replacement for Waxahachie's 1963-era downtown fire station, with the new facility rising on Spur 394.
topStories.body:
Waxahachie's oldest fire station is finally getting a successor. At its October 5 regular meeting, the City Council awarded Key Construction Texas LLC a guaranteed maximum price contract of $10,789,111 to build a new Fire Station #1 at 1475 Spur 394 — well south of the original 408 W. Main Street location that has been in service since 1963. Construction was scheduled to begin in October 2026 and is now under way.

The new station will be a 12,178-square-foot single-story building, designed to serve growth in the southern reaches of the city. Fire department leadership presented the plans to council and noted that the design went through several rounds of refinement to trim unnecessary square footage from earlier prototypes. The project scope includes site utilities, off-site roadwork, structural steel, HVAC, fire suppression systems, and apparatus bays, among other elements. Alternate pricing was also requested for an auxiliary apparatus storage building.

The land for the project was donated to the city by Waxahachie ISD, whose board voted in May 2026 to transfer approximately 3.1 acres. The old Main Street station, opened when the city had a fraction of its current population of roughly 53,500 residents, will continue operating until the new facility is complete.

topStories.headline: WISD's Global High School Wins $100,000 Federal Grant
topStories.dek: Waxahachie ISD's Global High School has been awarded a six-figure grant through the DART Foundation's Closing the Gap Project.
topStories.body:
Waxahachie ISD announced this fall that Global High School has been awarded a $100,000 grant through the DART Foundation's Closing the Gap Project. The district shared news of the award on its website, though detailed terms of the grant — including the precise date of award and the specific programs it will fund — have not yet been spelled out in publicly released documents.

Global High is Waxahachie ISD's alternative and accelerated learning campus, designed to serve students who benefit from a smaller, project-based setting. A grant of this size typically supports expanded coursework, technology, or student-support staffing. The WISD Board of Trustees is next scheduled to meet on November 10 at the district's central offices at 411 Gibson Street, where the grant and other business may be discussed. The public is welcome to attend.

events.title: WISD Board of Trustees Meeting
events.location: WISD Central Office, 411 Gibson Street, Waxahachie
events.description: The Waxahachie ISD Board of Trustees holds its regular monthly meeting. Members of the public may attend; check the district website for the posted agenda.

events.title: Waxahachie Community Development Corporation Meeting
events.location: Waxahachie Civic Center, 2000 Civic Center Lane, Waxahachie
events.description: The Waxahachie CDC holds its regular November meeting. Agendas are posted in advance on the city website.

events.title: 26th Annual Ellis County Veterans Celebration
events.location: Waxahachie Civic Center, 2000 Civic Center Lane, Waxahachie
events.description: The 26th annual ceremony honoring military veterans features live music, tributes, and a wreath-laying at the Ellis County Veterans Memorial, with a military-style flyover. The event runs through approximately 12:30 PM and is free and open to the public.

events.title: Ellis County Turkey Trot — 4th Annual
events.location: Getzendaner Park Trail, 400 S Grand Ave, Waxahachie
events.description: The fourth annual Thanksgiving morning run features a 5K, 10K, and 8-mile course along the Getzendaner Park Trail. Registration is $35; register by November 5 to guarantee a commemorative shirt and medal.

moreNews.headline: WHS Band and Color Guard Qualify for State Championships
moreNews.body: Waxahachie High School's band and color guard qualified for the Texas state championships, according to a November 3 report in the Waxahachie Daily Light. The achievement adds to an already strong fall season for Waxahachie ISD fine arts programs.

moreNews.headline: City Council Approves Agreement for Parks Master Plan Update
moreNews.body: The Waxahachie City Council voted at its November 2 meeting to approve an agreement to update the city's parks master plan, according to the Waxahachie Daily Light. The parks master plan guides long-range investment in the city's roughly 388 acres of park land.

moreNews.headline: Bowling Alley Fundraises to Help Veterans Get Service Dogs
moreNews.body: A Waxahachie bowling alley is raising money to help local veterans obtain service dogs, the Waxahachie Daily Light reported on November 5. Details on the specific organization being supported and how to donate were not fully available through open sources; readers can check with the Daily Light or the bowling alley directly.

restaurants.name: Ohana Sushi Ramen Poke

restaurants.name: Mariscos Muelle 77

hotels.description: A recently opened extended-stay hotel offering suites with full amenities, complimentary breakfast, and highly rated service.

hotels.name: Best Western Plus Waxahachie Inn & Suites
hotels.description: A well-regarded hotel offering complimentary breakfast, clean rooms, and friendly staff, popular with repeat visitors to Waxahachie.

shops.name: Kimmy's Boutique

shops.name: Sweet Peas Boutique

shops.name: Cheyenne Ranch Boutique
shops.description: A Western-flair retailer at the heart of Waxahachie's Historic Square offering cowboy-inspired clothing and accessories.

shops.name: Farmhouse

shops.name: Meat Church

artEntertainment.name: Waxahachie Community Theatre
artEntertainment.description: A nonprofit community theater company producing theatrical and musical performances for Ellis County audiences since 1979, with 2026 season shows at University Church in Waxahachie.

artEntertainment.name: Chautauqua Auditorium
artEntertainment.description: A National Register-listed 1902 octagonal auditorium seating 2,500 in Getzendaner Park, hosting the Fort Worth Symphony Orchestra, country music performances, community theater, and major civic events.
artEntertainment.address: 400 S Grand Ave (Getzendaner Park), Waxahachie, TX 75165

artEntertainment.name: Ellis County Art Association & Museum
artEntertainment.description: A nonprofit promoting visual arts in Ellis County, hosting member shows and exhibitions including the annual Sizzling Summer Art Show at the Beaudry Art Gallery on the downtown square.

artEntertainment.name: Scarborough Renaissance Festival

artEntertainment.name: Mosaic Madness

gymsRecreation.name: Waxahachie Country Club

gymsRecreation.name: Buffalo Creek CrossFit
gymsRecreation.description: A Waxahachie CrossFit affiliate offering group fitness classes and open gym with evening hours.
